```python
print((lambda f, y=10: f(y))(lambda x: x * 2, 5)) # 10 on both roads — the twin that names the slot

def apply(f, y=10):
    return f(y)
print(apply(lambda x: x + 1))                      # 11 in the reference; the same refusal, on the `def` road

print((lambda f, g=lambda v: v + 4: f(g(2)))((lambda n: n * 10)))  # 60 in the reference; exit 1 before
```

ADR 0370 registered the applied lambda as a higher-order body, which was the half the row owned; the entry-arity
audit then declined this one, because the call site does not name a tuple of functions for the defaulted slot, and the
ordinary road answered with ADR 0283's sentence about `"f"`. The answered twin beside it was the localisation: nothing
about the body differs, only the arity of the application. Two audits were in play, and both read the call's argument
list as the body's parameter list — `len(c.Args) != len(def.Params)` at the site loop, and the `Default != nil` drop in
`callableCalledParams`/`lambdaCalledParams`, which removed any defaulted parameter from `calledPos` before the first
audit could even be reached. That second rule was written when the pass had no way to name what a defaulted slot
holds, and the way turned out to exist: `resolve` answers an expression with the symbol of the function it names, so
a default that IS a function — an inline `lambda`, or a plain name — is an entry, and the omission is readable.

ADR 0371 made the tuple the body's. `callableSiteOmission` is the only arity audit a call is read against: every
position at or beyond the arguments written must have a default, and a called one must have a default that names a
function. `callableSiteOperand` resolves an omitted position from the parameter's own `Default` rather than from an
argument — the same expression the body would have seen, which is the only expression whose symbol can stand in the
body's call. `callableSiteFill` writes into the retargeted call the words the application left out, up to the last
position the body calls: the placeholder where the clone names the entry and reads nothing, a copy of the default's
expression where the body reads the slot (which is what the ordinary road would have evaluated for an omitted
argument anyway, ADR 0322), and nothing at or above the last called position, so the call road keeps sole ownership of
the default fill. `--callables` reports the count as `omitted_arguments`, because the two programs above are otherwise
indistinguishable in the emitted module.

The refusals the row leaves standing are named by shape rather than by the same sentence, which is the point of
paying a row instead of widening a refusal: an omitted CALLED slot whose default is not a function keeps the
value-word sentence (L11.1, ADR 0166 — the reference raises `TypeError: 'int' object is not callable` there, and asking
the value what it is needs the tag); an omitted READ slot whose default is a container, a `None` or a call keeps Gap
R.277's road, because binding an omitted container default arrives as a (payload, tag) pair and the entry tuple has
one word to carry it in; a keyword argument at such a site keeps the ordinary road, since reading it needs the
argument list reordered into positions, which is a different rewrite with its own trap; and a required parameter
after a defaulted one is the reference's own `TypeError`. Six sources went to the record from the reference
(7827 → 7833), and `integration/programs/lambda_applied_entry_tuple.gy` carries the family onto the matrix.

and that second clause is a hypothesis about the *wrong noun*. The scan is about the name the return
reads back; where that name came from is a different question, and a body that binds its own name to
`9.5` has no parameter to be blamed for. Nothing about the parameterless body makes the answer easier
to carry, either — the obstacle that forces a refusal in this family is a *parameter* whose word is a
heap handle or a `@str_tab` index, and that question is `doubleReturnCarriable`'s, which stayed put.
So removing the guard could not widen any refusal: for a body with no parameters the guard was not a
refusal, it was silence.

The second defect was behind the first, and the measurement that found it is the reason this is a row
rather than a one-line fix. With the guard removed, `u = 9.5` / `return u` answered `9.5`, but
`u = 2.5` / `v = u * 2` / `return v` still printed `0` — and so did the same body **with** a parameter,
which is the sign that the scan, not the parameter list, was the half that was broken:
`returnedFloatRebindings` asked `isFloat` of each name's binding ONCE, in Go's map order, with no
notion that `v`'s answer depends on `u`'s. Reach `v` first and the answer is no, and the function is
emitted with the truncated return word whatever the other binding says.

**Closed by ADR 0373 on 2026-10-19**, by two changes to that one function and one refactor beside it:

- The scan keeps the **last** binding of every name rather than asking whether any binding was ever a
  float, because the read answers the *last write's* word. That distinction is not decoration: an
  "was it ever a float" scan promotes `u = 2.5` / `u = 3` / `return u` and prints `3.0` where the
  reference prints `3` — the same class of wrong answer, pointed the other way. It is the rule
  `floatVars` already applies while emitting, read by the scan.
- The scan then settles its float table by **repetition**: each round snapshots the names it currently
  holds as doubles, asks every binding's question against that snapshot, and stops when a round moves
  nothing. `v = u * 2` is a double only once `u` is one, `u` is one only once its own binding is asked,
  and the snapshot is what keeps the result from depending on which order Go's map happens to iterate
  in (ADR 0273's determinism rule; the pass's own compile-twice test holds the same line from the
  other side).
- Each question is asked inside `(*irGen).withFloatNames`, the copy-add-restore of the float-variable
  table that `floatReboundReturnAsksForTheDouble` had been building privately. The scan and the
  emission now read one table, so `funcReturnsFloat`'s answer about a body, `isFloat`'s answer about
  one of its expressions, and the assignment road's decision while emitting cannot disagree — which is
  precisely the agreement whose absence produced the `define double` with an `ret i32` that ADR 0166
  counts as a rejected module. `emitClassMethod` passes the same helper, so a method and a function
  agree about what a float IS and differ only in what they can carry.

Left standing, and named rather than absorbed: a method whose body binds its own name to a double and
returns it still refuses, because a method's return word is fixed at `i32` together with the
receiver's; a dead `alloca double` survives in a body whose float binding is overwritten before the
return (the dead-allocation family, Gap R.290); and the module-wide `floatVars` map, which makes one
body's float binding decide another body's answer — **Gap R.339**, its own section below. The shape that
LOOKED like a third defect, `def twice(): return half() + half()`, answers `3.0` on both legs and is a
group of the conformance program: a callee's answer word is the callee's own question, and the caller
reads what the `define` says.

### Gap R.339 — the float-variable table is one map for a whole module, so one body's binding decides another's answer (closed by ADR 0375)

```python
def bound():
    u = 9.5
    return u          # 9.5 here too (ADR 0373)

def lastWrite():
    u = 2.5
    u = 3
    return u          # CPython 3 · this toolchain 3.0 — but 3 when the file holds ONLY this body

print(bound())
print(lastWrite())
```

The second body is the same program ADR 0373's own table answers `3` for. Written below a body that
binds the same NAME to a double, it answers `3.0`. Nothing in `lastWrite` changed; what changed is what
the file had emitted before it.

`g.floatVars` is the table every float question asks — `isFloat` for the print door, the arithmetic, the
negation, `logic_value`, `heapargs`, `list_index_kind`, `codegen_facts` — and the assignment road writes
into it ("this name's last write produced a double") as it emits. There is one per module, and no
statement clears it between `define`s. So the table is not "what is this body's name"; it is "what has
this toolchain seen since `main` started", and any predicate that reads it is answering a question about
one body with evidence from all of them.

Why it is a row and not a line: the fix is the table's SCOPE, and every reader of the table has to be
asked which question it is asking. The `saved`/`merged`/`restore` pair in `withFloatNames` — the helper
ADR 0373 extracted so a scan and an emission could not hold two opinions — is already the shape of the
per-body table; what is missing is installing a settled one at the moment each body's slots are decided,
instead of inheriting the previous body's history. A nested `lambda` then inherits its enclosing body's
table explicitly, which is the rule the closure road already uses for captured names.

The measure that keeps it honest is in the tracker's own artifact: `programs/float_answer_word.gy` was
written WITH this pair in it and the conformance matrix failed on it (`aot="…3.0…"` against
`python="…3…"`). The group was cut out of the asserted program rather than the ledger edited to accept
the wrong bytes, and the pair is pinned in
`pkg/lang/float_rebound_return_test.go::TestWhatTheFloatAnswerWordStillOwesIsFiledNotFixed` — reference
answer beside today's, exit 2 forbidden, and the row deleted when the two agree.

**Closed by ADR 0375 (2026-10-19).** The per-body table is installed by `enterBodyFloatTable`
(`pkg/lang/float_frame.go`) from the two places a body begins — `beginScope`, which already installs the
container, bool, None and interned-text tables for the same reason, and `enterBody`, which is the road the
method emitter and the closure lift take without calling `beginScope`. The frame's own map comes back on
the way out, so a nested `define` inherits its enclosing body's table *by restoration*, not by accident.
`funcDef` decides the return word through the new table, which is why the IR leg is part of the claim:
before, the int-returning body of `print(b(), a(), b())` opened `define double @gy_b()` — a function
returning a double it never computed — and the same `b()` answered `7.0` in one position of a `print` and
`7` in another.

What the row explicitly did NOT answer is whether a body may read a module-level float at all: that was
Gap R.35, and `RATE = 2.5` above `def scale(v): return v * RATE` refused, unchanged, with the module-state
sentence. `TestTheFrameRuleIsNotAnAnswerToTheModuleStateQuestion` pinned that refusal in the same file as
the fix, so the two rows could not be mistaken for one another by the next reader. **ADR 0376 has since
closed that half**: the two refusal rows this cycle pinned were deleted from that table and moved into the
answer table, which is how the guard knew, and what remains refused is the module CONTAINER — the half
Gap R.35 still owes, in `TestTheModuleFloatGateRefusesWhatItCannotPromise`. The `lastWrite`
pair is back in `programs/float_answer_word.gy`, the asserted program it was cut out of, and
`TestWhatTheFloatAnswerWordStillOwesIsFiledNotFixed` is deleted, as its own rule required.

Two defects surfaced by the same measurement were **filed below rather than absorbed here**: a `for`-driven
float accumulator inside a body (Gap R.341, since closed by **ADR 0377**) and a nested `def` that stores
through its enclosing frame's alloca (Gap R.342, since closed by **ADR 0378**). Both were identical on the
pre-ADR-0375 build, which is what made each of them a row rather than collateral.


### Gap R.336 — an entry that reads the frame its application is written in has no symbol to travel in (OPEN)

```python
def apply1(fn, v):
    return fn(v)

def use(seed):
    base = 1
    return apply1(lambda x: x + base, seed)   # 4 in the reference; exit 1 here

def twice(fn, seed):
    return fn(fn(seed))

def use_b(seed):
    base = 1
    return twice(lambda x: x * 2 + base, seed)  # 11 there; exit 1 here

def stepper():
    total = 0
    for step in [1, 2, 3]:
        shift = step * 10
        total = total + (lambda fn: fn(2) + shift)(lambda n: n * step)  # 72 there; exit 1 here
    return total
```

Each half alone answers: the same call with a self-contained entry (`apply1(lambda x: x + 1, seed)`) prints `4` at exit
0, and the same read written on the BODY side — `(lambda fn: fn(v) + base)(…)` — is Gap R.334's answered shape. So the
read is not the problem; the READ'S OWNER is. The pass declines, and its own account says so with the name attached:
`an entry lambda reads "base" from the frame its application is written in, and an entry is a bare symbol: the word that
name holds would have to arrive beside it (the capture parameter of the application road, asked on the entry side — Gap
R.336)`. That sentence is `callableLambdaFrameRead`'s, and it replaced a decline that said `a lambda passed to a
parameter reads that parameter's function` — true of nothing in these three programs, since `base` belongs to the caller
and not to the callee (ADR 0166's rule that a refusal names the missing thing).

Why it is a row and not a line: ADR 0345 made an ENTRY a symbol. `resolve` hoists a closed `lambda` to a module-level
`define` and the callee's body calls it by name; there is no value, no environment and no call site at that position
any more. A lambda that reads `base` cannot be hoisted and stay right — the read has to arrive as an argument — and the
only machinery that fills such an argument is the application road's capture parameter, which lives on the clone of the
APPLIED lambda, not on the callee. Threading it means the clone of `apply1`/`twice` carrying capture parameters of its
own, filled by ITS caller, which makes the clone's identity the pair (entry symbols, each entry's capture list) rather
than the tuple of entry symbols ADR 0345 and ADR 0364 hash today. Two applications of `twice` whose entries read
different frames are then two clones, and the recursion road's audit has to agree. The `stepper` spelling is the hard
case and it is in the table on purpose: the body side (`shift`) is R.334's and answers, the entry side (`step`) is this
row's, and the pass is all-or-nothing (ADR 0345), so one declined argument hands the WHOLE program to the ordinary road
— which is why the program's refusal is about `fn` at all.

### Gap R.337 — a decline the pass has a reason for reaches the reader as the ordinary road's generic sentence (closed by ADR 0379)

```console
$ gustyc --callables "$use_b_program"
{ "refused": ["defunctionalization declines: an entry lambda reads \"base\" … (Gap R.336)"] }
$ gustyc --file use_b.gy
gustyc: jit: codegen: "fn" is called but is not a function this backend can build a call to: … (roadmap L11.1, ADR 0166)
```

The pass knew. The terminal did not repeat it. `defunctionalizeCallables` swallows the `*callableDecline` and returns
the untouched program — the right rule for a REWRITE (all-or-nothing, ADR 0345) and a lossy one for a DIAGNOSTIC: the
emitter then meets a call to a parameter it was never told about and says what IT knows, which is ADR 0283's generic
sentence pointing at the memory-model row (L11.1) that owns nothing in the program. AGENTS.md's rule is that a refusal
names the missing machinery and the row that owns it, so a reader following the terminal goes to read the wrong ADR.
The fix is plumbing, not semantics — a decline carried out beside the program (never a package global: `make
testparallel` runs programs concurrently, ADR 0343) and appended to the uncallable-callable refusal when the call the
emitter cannot build is the one the pass declined over. It is filed rather than folded into ADR 0372 because it changes
no decision, and because ADR 0372's tables had to be written anyway: the answer tables pin what the compiled leg
PRINTS, the account tables pin what the pass SAYS, and the pair is the honest record until this row closes and the
terminal carries the second sentence too.

**Closed 2026-10-19 by ADR 0379.** The plumbing is three lines wide and one value deep. `defunctionalizeCallablesTelling`
runs the reading and the writing that `applyDefunctionalization` had always run and returns, beside the program, the
sentence the pass would tell about it — `""` when it rewrote the tree (there is nothing to explain about a rewrite) and
`""` when its only answer was the one it gives every first-order program in the corpus, which is why `t = 1` /
`print(t())` still gets ADR 0166's sentence with nothing appended to it. That second case is the one that makes this a
test and not a print: the 「nothing for me to do」 decline now carries a `noWork` mark on the `*callableDecline` itself,
so the question 「did the pass have work it wanted and fail?」 is asked of a field rather than decided by comparing prose.
`GenerateIRReport` copies the sentence onto that module's own `irGen.callablePassWord` — per-module state, not a package
variable, because the suite runs programs beside each other and a global there would let one compile answer another's
refusal; the case that pins it compiles a declined program and a no-work program alternately, in both orders, and asks
each message to stay its own. `callBuiltins` then QUOTES the sentence under a label that says who is speaking, in the
same bytes `--callables` prints in `refused` — the withdrawal (`the rewrite was withdrawn: …`), the second way a program
comes back untouched, became one function with one wording so both faces could not drift apart. Measured on the shipped
tool, both compiled roads:

```console
$ gustyc --eval use.gy
gustyc: jit: codegen: "fn" is called but is not a function this backend can build a call to: … (roadmap L11.1, ADR 0166)
  — the defunctionalisation pass (roadmap L11.7, ADR 0345) refused to rewrite this program before this call was ever
    reached, and said: defunctionalization declines: an entry lambda reads "base" from the frame its application is
    written in, and an entry is a bare symbol: … (Gap R.336) (roadmap L11.7, ADR 0345)
  — the same account prints beside `gustyc --callables <src>` (roadmap Gap R.337)
```

at exit **1**, with `--json` classifying the longer message as `lower.unsupported.indirect-call` exactly as the short one
was — the quotation is a quotation, not a new shape, and the classifier's most-specific-marker rule is pinned against it
for every row of both new files (ADR 0346's failure mode is an agent's branch that stops firing silently). What the row
demanded, and what the two files answer, is the trio: the citation reaches the terminal, the un-declined program keeps
its sentence byte for byte, and the account and the terminal agree in ONE run.

### Gap R.335 — a higher-order recursion that omits its own defaulted parameter is not a recursion the clone will follow (OPEN)

```python
def run(n, f=lambda x: x):
    return 0 if n == 0 else f(n) + run(n - 1)
print(run(3))            # 6 in the reference; exit 1 here
print(run(3, lambda x: x))  # 6 there too — naming every parameter is refused as well
```

The refusal is the ordinary road's `"f" is called but is not a function this backend can build a call to`, and the
account says what actually happened: `"run" recurses at line 2 without filling every parameter positionally, which a
clone cannot answer for the recursion` — ADR 0364's audit, the one clause of the omission rule **ADR 0371** did not
extend. Every other call of a higher-order function is now read against the body; a call of that function from inside
its own body still has to name every position, and that requirement is not mere conservatism. A clone is chosen by the
tuple of functions its called parameters are asked to be, and the recursion road follows a self-call by handing each
called parameter back to its own position (`fact(n, f)` calls `fact$tuple(n - 1, f)`, ADR 0364). A self-call that
writes fewer arguments than the body has parameters leaves that tuple with a hole — and the answer is not the ordinary
road's default fill, because for a CALLED slot the right word is the entry the enclosing clone was itself cloned for,
which is a fact about the clone rather than about the call site. The fix is therefore a small one with a real
distinction in it: read the self-site's tuple from the enclosing clone, and relax the audit to the one
`callableSiteOmission` already applies outside the body, so the two roads ask the same question of the same body.

### Gap R.330 — a capture three frames up has no call site to ask (OPEN)

```python
print((lambda x: (lambda y: (lambda z: x + y + z)(100))(10))(1))  # 111 in the reference; exit 1 here
print((lambda x: (lambda y: x + y)(1))(2))                        # 3 here — two frames, answered
```

The refusal is `lambda_2() reads "x" from the frame that encloses it, and that name holds a value no call in the
program can be asked about`. It is the gate working: ADR 0370 types a capture by asking every call of the frame what it
hands that parameter, and at this depth the name belongs to a frame that no call in the program names, so the question
has no answer to read and the gate refuses rather than carry a word whose kind it cannot state (ADR 0273). The fix is
to carry the capture through the frame that owns it — an intermediate `lambda` whose body applies another `lambda`
re-exports the names its own body is free in but does not bind, so the innermost capture is filled by the intermediate
call site and the outer frame is never reached directly. That is what a nested `def` does, and what the `collectNames`
`*Lambda` arm ADR 0370 added makes reachable.

### Gap R.331 — a `lambda` applied at module level whose body reads a non-number module name answers the payload word (OPEN)

```python
t = "hey"
print((lambda: t)())   # hey in the reference; 0 here, at exit 0
b = True
print((lambda: b)())   # True in the reference; 1 here, at exit 0
```

Not a regression from ADR 0370 — the pre-0370 binary prints the same two bytes — and not the capture gate's hole: a
module-level name is not a capture, so it reaches the body through the module-global road, and the print door
downstream of a call is never told the call answers a text or a bool. The same two programs written **inside a `def`**
are refused by ADR 0370's gate with the sentence that names L11.1, which is what localises this to the module road and
why the row is a return-kind registration rather than a new gate: `funcReturnsFloat` is the template ADR 0370 needed
to answer `print((lambda m: m / 2)(3))`, and the text and bool arms of the same question are missing for every body,
lambda or not. Both programs are on the record with the reference's `hey` and `True`, so the compiled leg cannot
silently keep the `0`.

### Gap R.332 — a captured name whose value is not a number has no word to travel in (OPEN)

```python
def f():
    xs = [1, 2]
    return (lambda: len(xs) + 1)()   # 3 in the reference; refused here
```

The text, bool and `None` forms refuse too, where the reference prints `hey`, `True` and `None`. ADR 0370's capture
parameters carry one `i32` — enough for a number, and for a function the pass has specialised into a name, which is
what the row owed. Every other kind would cross as a heap handle, a string-table index or a truncated number, which is
ADR 0273's failure wearing this row's coat, so `captureCarriesOneWord` asks the value tables the print door and the
arithmetic roads already read, **before** the body is emitted, and refuses. The refusal names the capture, the kind,
the road that would carry it (L11.1) and this row (L11.7 · Gap R.265, Gap R.276); it also names the two ways to write
the same program that do answer today — pass the value to the call, or write the body as a nested `def`. The fix is the
(payload, tag) pair ADR 0368 gives a call's answer, two words at the call site instead of one.

### Gap R.333 — a module-level text read inside a `lambda` body calls a runtime entry the module never defines, and exits 0 (OPEN)

```python
t = "hey"
print((lambda: t)())   # hey in the reference
```

The emitted body is:

```llvm
define i32 @gy_lambda_0() {
  %gc.frame.base = alloca i32
  call void @rt_frame_open(i32* %gc.frame.base)
  %t1 = call i32 @rt_str_intern2(i8* @.str1, i8* @.str2)   ; no define, no declare, anywhere
  ...
```

and `llc-20` answers, on both the linked module and the in-process-JIT module:

```
llc-20: error: /tmp/gusty-jit-…/jit.ll:8:18: error: use of undefined value '@rt_str_intern2'
```

The toolchain printed `0` and exited **0**. That is two defects standing in one program. The first is Gap R.2's, and
it has a guard already — `pkg/lang/runtime_block_emit_test.go` asserts that a module which *calls* `@rt_str_intern2`
*defines* it — but the guard covers the roads that register the runtime block, and the lambda body's module-name read
emits the call without registering anything. The second is ADR 0166's: a module `llc` rejects is an exit **2**, the
code that means "the compiler is broken", and it is not allowed to be the run a program got. `def f(): return "hey"`
above `print(f())` answers `hey`, which localises both halves to the lambda road's emission, and the pre-ADR-0370
build prints the same `0` at the same exit code, which is why the row is filed rather than folded into ADR 0370.

### Gap R.340 — a conditional expression ran the arm its test rejected (closed by ADR 0374)

```python
def boom():
    print("boom")
    return 1


x = 5
print(1 if x > 0 else boom())      # CPython `1`      · this backend printed `boom` then `1`
print(boom() if x < 0 else 2)      # CPython `2`      · this backend printed `boom` then `2`
print(1 if x > 0 else 1 // 0)      # CPython `1`      · ZeroDivisionError, exit 3 — from the dead arm


def fact(n):
    return 1 if n <= 1 else n * fact(n - 1)


print(fact(5))                     # CPython `120`    · "the compiled root stack is full", exit 2
```

The first two rows are ADR 0166's wrong-answer-at-the-exit-code-of-success; the third is a program that
dies of a raise it never performed; the fourth is the worst of the family, because the artifact was
*killed* rather than returning — the code the contract reserves for a broken compiler.

`--emit-llvm` named the cause on the spot. The whole conditional was one instruction whose operand list
contained the call:

```llvm
;t4 = icmp sgt i32 %_x.ld1, 0
%t8 = select (i1 %t7, i32 1, i32 %t5)      ; %t5 was produced by the call emitted above this line
```

A `select` has no unreachable operand. Both of its operands are *arguments*, which means the run time
executed both arms' instructions before the instruction chose between their results. ADR 0026 chose the
instruction, and the arms were lowered beside the test so that the `select` could take them as operands
— an arrangement that is only sound while an arm is a value.

ADR 0275 had already paid this for the two operators that choose an operand, `and` and `or`: evaluate the
first, branch on its truth, evaluate the second **only in the block the branch enters**, and meet the two
answers at a block-parameter `phi`. That ADR names the ternary as the second half of the same bug and
leaves it on the eager road. This is that half: `(*irGen).ternaryBranch` in `pkg/lang/ternary_arms.go` is
`logicSkeleton` for a test with two arms behind it, and the two lowerings that answer a ternary —
`ternaryI32` and `ternaryDouble` in `pkg/lang/ternary_number.go` — ask it before either arm is emitted.

The shape costs five labels (`tern.then`, `tern.else`, `tern.thenfwd`, `tern.elsefwd`, `tern.merge`), two
unconditional jumps, one `br i1` and one `phi` per answer. The two one-instruction forwarding blocks are
not decoration, twice over: a `phi`'s incoming block has to be a real predecessor and this generator
tracks no current-block state (ADR 0275's reason), and an arm that contains a call does not *end* where
the door left it — the call road closes with an `@exn_flag` test that branches to the enclosing
function's raise-exit or to a fresh continuation block, so the arm's last instruction lives in a block
this door did not name. Naming a forwarding block that the door owns, and having the arm jump to it, is
what makes both facts line up. It is also what makes a trap in a rejected arm impossible instead of
merely unobserved: the arm's raise unwinds to `main.raiseexit` with the frames the arm's own call pushed,
and `rt_die` prints `File "prog", line 2, in boom` for a raise the taken arm really performed.

Both arms are built into a **scratch builder**, and nothing reaches the caller until both answered — the
same rule ADR 0275 learned when a half-emitted door left a module with a block that had no terminator and
`llc` reported the compiler's mistake as the program's (Gap R.149).

**The gate is `ternaryArmsNeedBranch`, and "harmless" is a short list, not a long one.** An arm may still
be folded into the `select` when it provably cannot do anything except answer a value: a literal; a name
read the ADR 0228 written-flag machinery proves was written; `+ - * & | ^ << >>` over literals of one
domain and the six orderings over two literals that belong to the same domain; `not` and unary minus of a
literal. Everything else is "may act", because in this backend the ways an expression reaches the run
time are not a node type — a subscript raises `IndexError`/`KeyError`, `//` and `%` raise
`ZeroDivisionError`, an ordering of two kinds raises `TypeError`, a call raises and prints whatever its
body does, a container literal allocates, a comprehension loops. The first measurement of this row said
"the arm is a call", and that is the gate that would have shipped the third program above: `1 // 0`
raises with no call in sight, and so do `xs[9]` and `d["k"]`.

The written-slot question is asked from the same tables `checkBound` reads, which is not a performance
detail. An `UnboundLocalError` is an effect, and its guard cannot sit above the test: both operands of a
`select` dominate the test, so the flag is read for both arms whatever runs. Before this change

```python
def f(flag):
    if flag:
        y = 7
    return (1 if flag else y) + 0
```

raised for a name the taken arm never mentions, at exit 3, from the arm the program never reached.

**The fold stays.** Two literal arms, or arithmetic over literals, still produce the instruction ADR 0026
put here and ADR 0262 pinned, and `TestATernaryWithPureArmsIsStillASelect` asserts both halves of that —
the `select` is present *and* no `tern.merge` block exists. A pair of values has no effects to order, so
the two roads disagree about nothing except instruction count, and ADR 0273's rule is that a correctness
gate may not take an instruction away from a program that compiles and answers today.

What this row leaves to its neighbours, filed rather than smoothed over:

- **a container arm reaches the assembler as a global.** `[1, 2] if c > 0 else [3]` now lowers each
  literal beside its own branch, and the two arms meet at `phi i32 [ @.lst1, %tern.thenfwd ], [ @.lst2,
  %tern.elsefwd ]` — which is the same `i32 @.lstN` operand `llc` has rejected since Gap R.128 filed it,
  arriving through a `phi` instead of a `select`. The probe `programs/probe_ternary_container_arms.gy`
  keeps its per-leg pin; the answer is L11.1's tagged handle, not a fifth label.
- **arms that disagree on a word still refuse,** as ADR 0166 requires: `print(2 if x else 3.5)` says the
  arms do not agree on a word. Putting an arm behind a branch cannot promote it into a word it does not
  have, and the refusal is `L11.1`'s to earn.
- **a loop whose arm is a call pays the forwarding blocks on every pass**, which belongs to the
  block-placement family (Gap R.290's neighbourhood) and not to this defect: the answer is right, the
  module is five labels and three jumps per conditional.
### Gap R.341 — a `for`-driven float accumulator inside a body answered the void word (closed by ADR 0377)

```python
def loopAcc():
    t = 0.0
    for i in [1, 2, 3]:
        t = t + i
    return t

print(loopAcc())      # 6.0 in the reference, 0 here — at the exit code of success
```

The identical three lines at module level answer `6.0`, and that twin is a row of
`integration/programs/float_frame_table.gy`, so the difference is the BODY and not the accumulator: the
unrolled-`for` road and the body's `double` return word do not agree about where the running total lives.
Measured on 2026-10-19 while writing **ADR 0375**, and it is filed rather than folded into that row
because it answers the same before and after — the float table is per body now, and this shape's `0`
did not move, which is what localises it to the loop/return roads rather than to the table.

It cannot be recorded: `tools/recmerge` refuses a source whose compiled leg prints other bytes than the
reference's, so the pair is pinned in `pkg/lang/float_frame_test.go`
(`TestTheFrameRuleIsNotAnAnswerToTheModuleStateQuestion`) and `integration/float_frame_test.go`
(`TestWhatTheFrameRuleLeavesStandingIsFiledNotFixed`), each guarded to fail the day the program prints
`6.0` — a wrong value is exit 0's defect, never a refusal's, so the guard also fails if this becomes a
refusal.

### Gap R.342 — a nested `def` sharing a name with its enclosing body's float local stored through the enclosing alloca, and `llc` rejected the module (CLOSED by ADR 0378)

```python
def outer():
    def inner():
        w = 3
        return w
    w = 1.5
    return inner()

print(outer())        # 3 in the reference; here `llc-20` rejected the module and the program left exit 2
```

Inside `inner`, codegen emitted `store i32 %t7, i32* %_w` — and `%_w` was the ENCLOSING frame's alloca, so
the module the toolchain handed `llc` had a store through a slot that no `define` allocated:

```
llc-20: error: /tmp/gusty-jit-…/jit.ll:4347:23: error: use of undefined value '%_w'
  store i32 %t7, i32* %_w
```

Exit **2** is ADR 0166's code for a compiler bug, and an ordinary program the reference runs to completion
must not leave it. Renaming either binding compiled, which is the signature of a name-keyed table that one
road resets and another does not: `beginScope` resets `allocd` (「which slots exist」), and the closure lift
is the road that does not call it — it goes through `enterBody`, which since ADR 0375 installs the float
table but not the slot table. Measured the same on the pre-ADR-0375 build, so it was a row and not
collateral. The sibling to read beside it is **Gap R.274** (the nested `def`'s closure-slot global minted
with no owner in it) and **Gap R.49** (the same disease on the module side, cured by ADR 0351).

**The cure (ADR 0378) is the frame entry, in one file.** `pkg/lang/frame_slots.go` states the rule — a body
owns its own `allocd`, `gcRootSeen` and `freshSlots` — and hands out `enterFrameSlots`, which installs NEW
maps and returns the undo, so the enclosing frame's bookkeeping comes back whole (a nested body is emitted in
the *middle* of its frame's lowering; clearing the maps instead would have destroyed the record of slots the
enclosing frame still owns, which is what `emitFreeOld` and `copyInReboundParams` read). `enterBody` takes it,
`beginScope` delegates to it, and both body-emitting roads take it **before** the entry-block allocas: the
written-flag table (ADR 0228) had the identical hole one level down, because `emitBoundAllocas` writes the
allocas of whichever body's flags are installed and both roads asked it before installing their own.

**The probe, and the four shapes beyond the one that was filed.** Twenty programs on one axis — *which frame
owns the name* — each asked of the compiled leg and the reference. Five reached exit 2:

| shape | `llc` said | the reference |
|---|---|---|
| nested `def` sharing a float-named local | `use of undefined value '%_w'` | `3` |
| nested `def` with a possibly-unwritten local | `use of undefined value '%bnd_z'` | `UnboundLocalError` |
| method with a possibly-unwritten local | `use of undefined value '%bnd_z'` | `UnboundLocalError` |
| nested `def` binding the container its enclosing body binds | `use of undefined value '%_xs'` | `11` |
| nested `def` binding the text its enclosing body binds | `use of undefined value '%_s'` | `7` |

Two of the five were container and text collisions rather than float ones, which is the measurement that says
the fault was the frame entry and not the float convention — and the container/text rows had been *wrong
answers* (`0`) at Gap R.332's road, which is why they are not the same row. The two unwritten-local rows now
raise what the reference raises, catchably, at exit 3 (`TestTheUnwrittenLocalTrapIsTheProgramsExceptionNotThe
Compilers`), which is ADR 0214's distinction: a frame slot the compiler owns versus a raise the program owns.

**The audit, so the rule cannot rot back.** `pkg/lang/frame_audit.go` walks the shipped module — after
`attachFrameStack`, before `hoistAllocas` — and asks of each `define` whether every slot-shaped pointer operand
it reads (`%_…`, `%_…_tag`, `%_ctr…`, `%bnd_…`) was allocated by an `alloca` in *that* function. Its failure is
`*lang.IRInvariantError`, classified by the CLI exactly like an `llc` rejection: exit 2, and under `--json` the
`invariant` object naming the audit, the function, the slot and the instruction (`definitions.irInvariant`).
`llc` already caught this class; what it could not do was say which function, which slot, or whose fault it
was — it named a file under `/tmp`. Asked only when nothing else refused, so a program the compiler declined
is still reported as the refusal it got.

What the fix deliberately does **not** do is seed a nested body's table from the enclosing frame: a captured
name travels in the environment (`%env`), not in the enclosing frame's dead stack slots, and sharing the cell
would be ADR 0351's 「per scope」 deleted. Three shapes the same probe reached stay filed instead: **Gap
R.345** (a lifted `def` whose body answers a double), **Gap R.346** (two nested `def`s of one spelling), and
**Gap R.332**/**R.337** (a `def` nested inside a *method* is not lifted at all).

Witnesses: `pkg/lang/frame_slots_test.go` (answers, traps, catchability, the IR rows that pair each store with
the `alloca` in the same `define`, the audit asked directly with forged and legal modules, the wiring rows, and
`TestTheFrameEntryIsAnEntryAndNotARename` asked of the Go value), `integration/frame_slots_test.go` (both
compiled legs against CPython, **exit 2 in any row is a failure of the file**), `cmd/gustyc/ir_invariant_test.go`
(the class and the payload), the asserted conformance row `integration/programs/nested_def_shares_a_slot.gy`, and
15 record entries added through `tools/recmerge`. The two exit-2 rows that pinned this defect —
`TestTheFrameRuleIsNotAnAnswerToTheModuleStateQuestion` and `TestWhatTheFrameRuleLeavesStandingIsFiledNotFixed`'s
R.342 case — were deleted as their own text required.


### Gap R.345 — a lifted `def` whose body answers a double answers `0` at exit 0 (OPEN)

```python
def outer():
    def inner():
        w = 1.5
        return w
    w = 3
    return inner()

print(outer())        # 1.5 in the reference; 0 here, at the exit code of success
```

ADR 0378 gave the lifted closure its own slot, and the slot is the right shape — the module says so:

```
define internal i32 @inner_env(i32 %env) {   # the lift opens itself, whatever the body computes
  %_w = alloca double                        # the closure's own slot, correctly its own
  %t1 = fadd double 0.0, 1.5e+00
  store double %t1, double* %_w
  %_w.ld1 = load i32, i32* %_w               # read back through the low word
  ret i32 %_w.ld1                            # → 0
}
```

This is ADR 0377's return-word fold **unwritten on this one road**: the `def` road folds the body's writes to
choose `define double` vs `define i32`, and the closure lift has never asked the question — it opens
`define internal i32 …_env(i32 %env)` unconditionally, and the trampoline beside it too (the half Gap R.341's
row named as next-open). The frame entry is not the fix and did not change it: the row is identical on the
pre-ADR-0378 build. The inverse shape — the nested body taking the int and the enclosing body the float — is
the one Gap R.342 closed, so the two rows together say the lift road still has a word question to answer.

Pinned as a filed row by `pkg/lang/frame_slots_test.go`'s `TestWhatTheFrameEntryLeavesStandingIsFiledNotFixed`,
whose message moves the source into the answer table the day it prints `1.5`. It cannot be recorded: the
record's entry is the reference's answer, and `tools/recmerge` refuses a source whose compiled leg disagrees.


### Gap R.346 — two nested `def`s of the same spelling in two frames collide on the global the lift mints (OPEN)

```python
def a():
    def inner():
        return 1
    return inner()

def b():
    def inner():
        return 2
    return inner()

print(a() + b())      # 3 in the reference; here exit 2
```

```
llc-20: error: redefinition of global '@inner_slot'
@inner_slot = internal global i32 0
```

The closure lift mints one `internal global` per closure to hand the closure's environment cell a name, and
mints it from the closure's *spelling* alone — so two `def inner` in two unrelated frames mint the same symbol
twice and the module is malformed before anyone looks at the values. Verified identical on the pre-ADR-0378
build, which is what makes it a row rather than this cycle's collateral: no frame-entry change mints or names
globals. It is ADR 0228's minting read without an owner, the same shape **Gap R.274** filed for the nested
`def`'s slot global — the minted name needs the frame that owns it in the name, which is also why this program
cannot be written twice in one file today.

Found by writing the cycle's conformance program: the first draft named two nested `def`s `inner`, and the
program died in `llc` before the frame rule was ever exercised. Pinned by
`TestWhatTheFrameEntryLeavesStandingIsFiledNotFixed` (its `dies` row fails when the module starts to compile),
and `integration/programs/nested_def_shares_a_slot.gy` renames one binding and says why in its comments.

### Gap R.35 — a compiled function body reads the module's float; the module's container is still owed (PARTIAL, float half closed by ADR 0376)

ADR 0227 built the mechanism and left a hole in it on purpose: `moduleSlots` maps a name to an `i32`
global, a double does not fit an `i32`, and so every module-level float a body named was answered with the
module-state refusal — exit 1, at a program CPython runs. The refusal was honest and it was also the last
place in the float family where the module had no word, once ADR 0373 had settled which write a read
answers and ADR 0375 whose.

ADR 0376 gives the double the sibling it was missing: `@gy_mod_<NAME> = global double`, written by `@main`
in source order and loaded by any body that reads the name without binding it. The gate is what makes that
safe, and it is written as a *rejection* list rather than an allowance, because the compiler can promise a
word only for a number it can see:

- every module binding of the name is a float literal, a negated one, or arithmetic over literal numbers
  (`RATE = 7 / 2`, `AREA = 2.0 * 3`, and `RATE = RATE * 2` — the module doubling what it already holds,
  which `@main` replays in the order the source wrote);
- nothing else binds the name — no `for` target, `with ... as`, `match` capture, unpacking, `import`;
- no body that reads the name also writes it (ADR 0220), and no parameter carries it;
- it is not a folded module constant already (a name bound once to a literal is a value, and ADR 0227's
  fold is cheaper than a global; `TestTheModuleFloatIsAGlobalAndNotAnAlloca` keeps that control, together
  with the one that says a module float no body reads keeps its alloca byte for byte).

The two roads are deliberately unequal, and that inequality is the design: `floatValue` loads the global,
`valueName` (the i32 road) refuses the name, because one i32 slot, `select` or `ret` cannot carry a double
and emitting the load anyway is the `mul i32 %p1, <double>` that `llc` rejects at exit 2. A method is
refused before its `define` is written — a method has an i32 return word whatever its body computes, which
is ADR 0196's rule about a rebound parameter, extended to the module's double — and a nested `def` is
refused by the i32 road's sentence, which names the body so the reader learns the same expression in a
top-level `def` does compile.

What stays owed, in the same table as the answers: a module-level **container** read by a body. A
container's word is a heap handle, which has to be rooted against the collector, and its element
operations come from the per-scope notebooks ADR 0341 settles at a *binding*; a global handle buys none of
that, and a half-working container is exactly the trade this repo refuses. `xs = [1, 2, 3]` above
`def f(): print(xs)` therefore still refuses, and `TestTheModuleFloatGateRefusesWhatItCannotPromise` keeps
that refusal beside the eleven shapes that now answer, so "half closed" cannot be read as "closed".

### Gap R.343 — a module-level TEXT read by a compiled body answers the intern position (OPEN)

Filed while writing ADR 0376's tables, and identical on the pre-ADR build: `NAME = "world"` above
`def greet(): print(NAME)` prints **`0`** at exit 0 where the reference prints `world`. It is the same door
as Gap R.35 with the other half of ADR 0227's word list: `moduleSlotNames` admits a name whose module
bindings are "scalar", an interned text is an index, the index travels through the `i32` global correctly,
and the print road downstream of the load is never told the `i32` it is holding is an index into
`@str_tab` — so it prints the number, which is `0` for the first interned literal.

Two things make it a row rather than a footnote. It prints at exit **0**, which is the class of defect this
repo files rather than ships (ADR 0166, ADR 0273); and the cure is not the float door — a text needs the
`internedVars` marking a parameter carries (Gap R.315, ADR 0366) to reach the print, `str`/`repr`, `len`,
`in`, `==` and formatting doors, which is per-body state the module road does not have. The ADR 0227 slot
is fine; what is missing is the kind on the other end of it.

Pinned by `TestWhatTheModuleTextDoorStillOwes`, which asserts today's `0` and the reference's `world`
beside it and fails the day the two agree.

### Gap R.344 — printing a float-returning call whose argument arrives as a double emits an i32 store of a double, and `llc` rejects the module (OPEN)

Filed while writing ADR 0376's tables, and identical on the pre-ADR build — none of these programs mentions
a module float at all:

```
def f(v):
    return v + 1.0
print(f(2.0))          # reference 3.0 · this toolchain: llc-20 rejects the module, exit 2
```

`f` is promoted correctly (`define double @gy_f(double %p0, ...)`) and the call is emitted correctly
(`call double`); what is missing is the *answer* word. `return v + 1.0` is a shape ADR 0254's return-kind
table does not register, so the `print` downstream takes the tagged-value road and emits
`store i32 %t8, i32* %t105` with `%t8` a `double` — a module `llc-20` refuses, which ADR 0166 makes exit
**2**, the code reserved for a compiler bug, on an ordinary program the reference runs in three lines.

Where the boundary falls is measurable and narrow: `return v * 2`, `return v`, `return v + 1` and
`return RATE * 2` all answer the reference, while `return v + 1.0`, `return 2.0 * v` and
`return v * 2.0` reach the bad `store`. It is the promoted parameter meeting a *literal float in the
returned expression* that has no registered answer kind. The shapes ADR 0376's programs use are the ones
the table answers, which is why the conformance legs are green while this row is open.

Pinned as an exit-2 row by `TestWhatTheFloatAnswerWordOfACallStillOwes`, which fails — in either direction
— the day the program stops dying in `llc`.


The cure, and the line it had to walk (ADR 0377). `returnedFloatRebindings` is the scan that says, before
any instruction exists, which of a body's names end up holding doubles — because the answer picks the
`define`'s return word, its parameter words, and the convention every call site emitted earlier is already
committed to (ADR 0273's reason the scan exists at all). ADR 0373 made it ask the **last** write, which is
right for `u = 2.5` / `u = 3` / `return u` — and silent for an accumulator, because the last write of a
loop accumulator reads the very name whose kind is being decided. `isFloat(t + i)` looked up `t`, found an
empty table and an int loop variable, and the body was emitted `define i32`; the IR then showed the whole
mistake in two lines, a `store double` into the accumulator's slot and a `load i32` out of it.

The fix folds the writes in source order and asks each one against the kinds the earlier ones produced, so
a newest write that **states** a kind still decides (`u = 2.5` then `3` → int; a float accumulator later
rebound to `3` → int) and a newest write that **inherits** one (`t = t + i`) is asked with the kind the
seed gave it. Four rows in `floatFramePrograms` hold all four corners of that table, two of them being
precisely the cases ADR 0373 exists for — which is the reason the fold was chosen over the tempting
"was it ever a float" seeding, the one change that would have quietly reopened R.338 and printed `3.0`.
